In [[27 BBY/Legends|27 BBY]], a '''skirmish''' occurred between the ''[[Springhawk/Legends|Springhawk]]'', a [[Starship/Legends|vessel]] of the [[Chiss Expansionary Fleet/Legends|Chiss Expansionary Fleet]]'s [[Picket Force Two/Legends|Picket Force Two]], and a [[Vagaari plunder ship]], along with its two [[Vagaari starfighter|fighter]] escorts. The plunder ship made its way into the [[Crustai system/Legends|Crustai system]] on the edges of the Chiss Ascendancy, where a [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]] [[Sentry droid/Legends|sentry]] disabled its [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]]. The ''Springhawk'', under the [[Commander/Legends|command]] of Chiss [[Force Commander]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Mitth'raw'nuruodo]], quickly destroyed the [[Starfighter/Legends|fighters]] and approached the plunder ship. The commander boarded the Vagaari ship with his crew, secured the vessel, and found a large storage area full of treasure from various [[Planet/Legends|worlds]]. The Chiss then transported the plunder ship to the [[Crustai asteroid base|Crustai base]], where the [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Dubrak Qennto]] helped Mitth'raw'nuruodo take an inventory of the treasure on the ship.

==Prelude==
{{Quote|He did a microjump.''"<br />"''Ridiculous, you can't hit the side of the Senate Building with a&hellip;''"<br />"''I'd say he did a little better than hit the side of the Senate Building. Looks like he's right where he wants to be.''"<br />"''Terrific. I'm glad ''he'' wants to be here.|Jorj Car'das and Dubrak Qennto, discussing Thrawn's microjump|<ref name="Outbound Flight (novel)" />}}
In [[27 BBY/Legends|27 BBY]], [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]] [[Force Commander]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Mitth'raw'nuruodo]] of the [[Chiss Expansionary Fleet/Legends|Chiss Expansionary Fleet]]'s [[Picket Force Two/Legends|Picket Force Two]] impounded a [[Light freighter/Legends|light freighter]], the ''[[Bargain Hunter]]'', which was [[Captain/Legends|captained]] by [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Dubrak Qennto]] and crewed by [[Jorj Car'das]] and [[Maris Ferasi]]. The smugglers were brought aboard the ''[[Springhawk/Legends|Springhawk]]'', a [[Cruiser/Legends|cruiser]] under the [[Commander/Legends|command]] of Mitth'raw'nuruodo&mdash;known to the smugglers by his [[Core name/Legends|core name]]: Thrawn. The ''Springhawk'' began to travel back to the [[Crustai asteroid base|Crustai base]], Thrawn's headquarters. However, before it arrived, Thrawn was alerted to the presence of strangers in [[Chiss Ascendancy/Legends|Chiss space]] and the ''Springhawk'' preformed a [[Precision hyperspace jump|micro-jump]] that lasted less than a [[Standard minute/Legends|minute]] to confront the intruders.<ref name="Outbound Flight (novel)" />

==The skirmish==
{{Quote|I merely noticed that in both of their attacks a laser salvo preceded their missiles in a distinct and predictable pattern. When they launched their third attack, I was able to fire back just as the tubes' protective doors opened, detonating the missiles before they could be launched. Fighters that size never have sufficient armor to withstand that sort of internal blast.|Thrawn, describing how he destroyed two Vagaari fighters|<ref name="Outbound Flight (novel)" />}}
[[File:Outboundthrawn.jpg|thumb|300px|right|Force Commander Mitth'raw'nuruodo]]
As the ''Springhawk'' returned to [[Realspace/Legends|realspace]], two small [[Vagaari starfighter|Vagaari fighter]]s flew past the [[Viewport/Legends|viewport]], shooting [[Laser/Legends|laserfire]] and [[Missile/Legends|missiles]]. The fighters were protecting a [[Vagaari plunder ship]] whose [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] had earlier been disabled by a Chiss [[Sentry droid/Legends|sentry]]. The [[Vagaari/Legends|Vagaari]] were [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]] that Thrawn had only heard about before, as they had never previously entered Chiss space. The [[Starfighter/Legends|fighters]] quit firing as they flew out of their optimum range, but they soon came back around for another pass, this time one on each side of the ''Springhawk''. However, Thrawn had noticed a pattern in the fighters' shooting and was able to predict their next move. He shot the ''Springhawk''{{'s}} weapons at the fighters, hitting the port from which their missiles were just about to launch, detonating the missiles before they were ejected and exploding the fighters.<ref name="Outbound Flight (novel)" />

The ''Springhawk'' then turned to the plunder [[Starship/Legends|ship]] in the background. The Vagaari ship fired four salvos of missiles at the cruiser, but the Chiss vaporized the missiles in midflight. The ''Springhawk'' then approached the plunder ship while Qennto, Ferasi, and Car'das returned to their quarters. Thrawn boarded the enemy ship with his warriors and attacked the Vagaari. Even though the ''Springhawk''{{'s}} [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|bridge]] crew did not board with the others, they helped the boarding party by tracking the Vagaari combatants aboard the plunder ship with the ''Springhawk''{{'s}} [[Sensor/Legends|sensors]] and informing the boarders where their enemies were, resulting in many Vagaari [[Death/Legends|deaths]].<ref name="Outbound Flight (novel)" />

==Aftermath==
{{Quote|A treasure vessel, carrying the plunder of many worlds. They were not only slavers, but pirates and raiders as well.''"<br />"''You sound like you already know these people.''"<br />"''Only by reputation. At least, up until now.''"<br />"''You've been hunting them?''"<br />"''Of course not, The Vagaari have made no move against the Chiss Ascendancy. We therefore have no reason to hunt them.|Thrawn and Car'das, upon entering the Vagaari plunder ship's treasure room|<ref name="Outbound Flight (novel)" />}}
The Chiss secured the vessel within an [[Standard hour/Legends|hour]], and two hours after that, Qennto, Ferasi, and Car'das were brought aboard the ship. A Chiss warrior led them through the dead bodies and other carnage to Thrawn, who told them that the Vagaari were [[Slavery/Legends|slavers]] and pirates. He led them into a storage room filled with bins, cabinets, and treasure of all kinds: [[ingot]]s, [[Coin/Legends|coins]], gems, artwork. Thrawn had the vessel towed back to the Crustai base for further study.<ref name="Outbound Flight (novel)" />

Later, Chiss [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Ar'alani/Legends|Ar'alani]] arrived at the Crustai base with Thrawn's brother, [[Mitth'ras'safis/Legends|Mitth'ras'safis]]. Ar'alani believed that Thrawn should not have attacked the Vagaari, because they had not yet done any harm to the Chiss Ascendancy itself, although they had attacked and enslaved many other [[Species/Legends|species]]. Thrawn transported her, his brother, Car'das, and Ferasi to the Vagaari plunder ship. When they arrived, Thrawn took them on a tour of the ship. The Admiral was surprised to see Qennto in the treasure room and demanded to know what he was doing there. Thrawn explained that he was taking an inventory of the treasure and was choosing what he would like to take with him as payment. Ar'alani chose to stay and take an inventory herself while Thrawn tended to a report he had received of more Vagaari nearby. Shortly after, Thrawn's forces [[Battle of Geroon|stole]] a
Vagaari [[Gravity well projector/Legends|gravity well projector]] during the Vagaari attack on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Geroon]].<ref name="Outbound Flight (novel)" />

==Behind the scenes==
The skirmish in the Crustai system first appeared in [[2006]]'s [[Outbound Flight (novel)|''Outbound Flight'']] by [[Timothy Zahn]], but it was not given a name in the novel.<ref name="Outbound Flight (novel)" />
